lots.what_it_is: Six small 800-standard silver footed bowls (catalogued as finger bowls), 4.5 cm high by 12 cm diameter, 758.2 g total. Each has a different embossed centre: rampant lion, double-headed eagle, sword crossing two shields with a ribbon, palm tree, three lions passant on a shield, winged lion of St Mark. Continental, maker unidentified, probably 20th century.
lots.score_reason: The metal alone is worth about $1,700 at spot (606.6 g fine silver). There is no verified sale of a comparable set, so the score rests on melt, discounted for scrap payout (usually well under spot) and for not having confirmed the mark on all six.

lots.what_it_is: Brass reflecting circle of Troughton's pattern (pierced lattice frame, three turned wooden handles, index and horizon mirrors, silvered scale with vernier and tangent screw), signed on the arms 'Troughton' / 204 / 'London', with five telescopes or sight tubes and a key, in a worn dovetailed mahogany box. Edward Troughton, London, about 1796 to 1826.
lots.score_reason: The signature is read and the instrument type matches Troughton's own reflecting circle design, which is a scarce and collectable navigation instrument. I could not verify a single price (sold, unsold or asking), so the score is held at 7 for lack of evidence and the unknown completeness and possible later box.
